persona.name: Lakshmamma
persona.about: About 50. Keeps 14 goats, 4 sheep and one Hallikar-cross cow on 2 acres of ragi. Husband works in Bengaluru on weekdays, so she handles the animals alone. Studied to 5th standard. Speaks simple Indian English mixed with Kannada words (aadu = goat, kuri = sheep, hasu = cow, mari = kid/young one, jwara = fever, bedi = loose motions, haalu = milk, amma/madam/sir to the operator). Tired and worried, but polite.
persona.phone_how: Says it in groups, the way people do: 'nine nine zero zero one... two three four five six'. If asked for 'this number', says yes, this same phone.

cases.title: Three goats with loose motions (routine)
cases.opening: Namaskara... my goats are having loose motions.
cases.story: Three goats have watery loose motions (bedi) for three days. They are still standing, walking, breathing fine, eating a little less. She gave turmeric water. No deaths.
reveal_only_if_asked: They started after she grazed them near the tank where water collected after rain.
Eating a little less than usual.
No blood in the dung.
cases.source: Diarrhoea is the top recorded cause of goat deaths in village studies (Madhya Pradesh, 2013; Tamil Nadu Cauvery delta, 2022).

cases.title: Goats sick after buying new ones at the shandy; one kid died (urgent)
cases.opening: Hello? Madam... my goats are not well. One small one died this morning.
cases.story: Ten days ago she bought three goats at the Kanakapura Sunday santhe. Four days ago her goats started getting sick; now five are sick. They have fever (ears and body hot), thick discharge from eyes and nose, sores inside the mouth so they are not eating, and since yesterday loose motions. One kid (mari) died this morning. They can stand but are very dull. Two of them breathe fast with a cough. She has given nothing except some neem leaves. Her goats were never vaccinated for anything.
reveal_only_if_asked: Bought three goats at the Kanakapura santhe ten days ago (only if asked about new animals, buying, or where the animals came from).
Sores in the mouth, bad smell from the mouth (only if asked about eating, the mouth, or what else she sees).
Eyes and nose discharge (only if asked about the eyes, nose, or what else).
Not vaccinated (only if asked about vaccination).
The neighbour's goats are fine so far.
cases.manner: Upset about the dead kid. Starts with the death and 'not well', and does not list symptoms by herself: gives one sign at a time.
cases.source: Karnataka PPR outbreaks 2014-15 were traced to animals newly brought in from other flocks; young animals hit hardest (Indian outbreak investigation; PMC10000058 on PPR in Karnataka).

cases.title: Goats ate young jowar sprouts, trembling and breathing fast (urgent, minutes matter)
cases.opening: Madam, madam, quickly... my goats are shaking, one has fallen.
cases.story: About an hour ago four goats got into the neighbour's field and ate young jowar (sorghum) sprouts that came up after the rain. Now all four are trembling, breathing very fast and hard, frothing at the mouth. One has fallen and cannot get up; the other three are standing. She has not given anything.
reveal_only_if_asked: They ate young jowar sprouts in the neighbour's field (only if asked what they ate, where they grazed, or what happened before).
It was about one hour ago.
Frothing at the mouth (only if asked about the mouth or what else).
cases.manner: Panicky and fast. Short broken sentences. Not sure of the count at first ('four... I think four').
cases.source: Feeding immature sorghum is the commonest cyanogenic plant poisoning of livestock in India, and goats are the most susceptible ruminants (Pashu Sandesh on cyanide toxicity; cyanide deaths of 56 cows on sorghum sprouts in Guntur).

cases.title: A healthy goat found dead, another kicking at its belly (urgent)
cases.opening: Sir... one of my good goats died in the night. It was fine yesterday.
cases.story: Her fattest young goat was found dead this morning with no sign of illness the day before. Now a second young goat is lying down, kicking at its belly, grinding its teeth and making noise; it cannot get up. Yesterday she let them graze on her brother's harvested field and gave them extra horse gram (huruli) because there was some left over. The rest look normal. Breathing of the sick one: she is not sure, maybe fast. She gave nothing.
reveal_only_if_asked: Grazed a harvested field and got extra horse gram yesterday (only if asked about feed, grazing, or what changed).
Not vaccinated (only if asked).
The dead goat's belly was swollen.
cases.manner: Quiet, shocked. Talks about the dead goat first; mentions the second sick goat only when asked if others are sick or how many.
cases.source: Enterotoxaemia (sudden death after a change to rich feed or grain) is among the kid and goat deaths in Indian owner-recall studies (West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, 2015).

cases.title: Two small kids coughing and not suckling in the cold (routine, may turn urgent)
cases.opening: Namaskara madam. My small ones have a cold, I think.
cases.story: Two kids, about one month old, have been coughing with a running nose for four days. Since yesterday they are not suckling well, and one is breathing fast with its belly moving a lot. They can stand. The nights are cold and the shed is open on one side. Their mothers are fine. She gave them warm water with a little jaggery.
reveal_only_if_asked: The shed is open on one side and nights are cold (only if asked about housing or the shed).
One kid breathes fast with the belly moving (only if asked about breathing).
Mothers are fine.
cases.manner: Thinks it is a simple cold and asks which tablet to give. Pushes once for a medicine name.
cases.source: Pneumonia and diarrhoea are the top causes of kid deaths, highest at 0-3 months and in winter (Chambal, Madhya Pradesh, 2013; Cauvery delta, Tamil Nadu, 2022).

cases.title: The cow's milk has dropped and lumps are coming up on her skin (routine, notifiable)
cases.opening: Madam, my cow is giving very less milk from two days.
cases.story: Her one cow (Hallikar cross) dropped from four litres to one litre of milk. She has fever, and round lumps have come up all over the skin, neck and legs, since three days. Her front legs are swollen so she walks slowly, but she can stand. Breathing is fine. Two cows in the next street have the same lumps. There are many flies and mosquitoes. She applied turmeric paste on the lumps.
reveal_only_if_asked: Lumps all over the skin (only if asked what else, about the skin, or the body).
Neighbours' cows have the same (only if asked about other animals in the village).
Not vaccinated this year.
cases.manner: Talks about the milk first, because that is her income. Only mentions the lumps when asked what else she sees.
cases.source: Lumpy skin disease, 2022: fever and skin nodules, lameness, milk production crashed (Down To Earth from Malkisar, Bikaner; Scroll.in on Rajasthan's 21% milk drop).

cases.title: A goat straining to deliver for two hours, one leg showing (urgent)
cases.opening: Madam, my goat is trying to give birth... it is not coming.
cases.story: One goat has been straining to deliver for about two hours. Only one front leg of the kid is showing. The goat is now lying down, crying, and getting tired; she cannot get up. Breathing heavy from straining. It is her first kidding. Lakshmamma tried pulling the leg a little with oil on her hands.
reveal_only_if_asked: Only one leg is showing, not the head (only if asked what she can see).
First kidding for this goat.
She pulled a little with oil on her hands (only if asked what she did or tried).
cases.manner: Anxious, keeps asking 'should I pull?'. Needs to be told to wait for the vet team.
cases.source: Obstetric emergencies (dystocia) are a standing category of 1962 ambulance-veterinary calls (EMRI GHS).
